t: You're standing in Langham Place, off Regent Street, where St. George's Hall once stood. It was a theatre, built in 1867 and closed in 1966. It held up to nine hundred people, or fifteen hundred with the galleries. The architect was John Taylor of Whitehall. The stage magician and inventor John Nevil Maskelyne lived and died here. He worked with the magicians George Alfred Cooke and David Devant, and many of his illusions are still performed today. In 1914 he founded the Occult Committee to investigate claims of supernatural power.
